content: A birthmark is a skin blemish that forms before birth. These marks are classified as part of a group of skin lesions known as naevi. The exact cause of birthmarks remains unknown, but potential factors may include cellular damage caused by exposure to radiation or chemicals. Certain types of birthmarks appear to have a hereditary component, as they tend to run in families. In Italian and Middle Eastern cultures, birthmarks are referred to as voglie in Italian or wiham in Arabic, both of which translate to wishes. According to folklore, these marks are believed to result from the unfulfilled wishes or cravings of the mother during pregnancy. For instance, if a pregnant woman experiences a sudden craving for strawberries and does not satisfy it, it is said that the infant may develop a strawberry-shaped birthmark. There are several types of birthmarks, including but not limited to stork bites, Mongolian blue spots, strawberry marks, café au lait spots, congenital melanocytic naevi, and port-wine stains.
